conclusion: At full duration, defense weight 1.5 was the useful shaping setting; weight 2 raised mean slightly but reduced worst-side robustness. The 1.5 comparison follows a slight-shaping predecessor and isolates defense weight; stochastic replication is absent.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Establish the full-length combined-heuristic control without potential shaping.

results_insights.insight: The unshaped full-length control reached 35.5% average win rate.
Its weakest policy/side win rate was 3%.
Defensive-X competence reached 60%, paired with 14.75-move games.
The defensive-X win rate was observed over moderate-length games.

reasoning: Long combined-heuristic exposure produced moderate average strength without shaping.
The 3% floor indicates the combined/opponent-side weaknesses remained substantial.
This control defines several regimen knobs at once relative to earlier curricula, so only later within-group variants isolate shaping.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether slight potential shaping improves the full combined-heuristic control.

results_insights.insight: Slight shaping reduced average win rate from 35.5% to 27%.
Defensive-X fell from 60% to 30%, with 15.6-move games.
Episode length was similar to control, while wins halved.

reasoning: A 0.005 shaping coefficient without defense bias harmed aggregate and defensive performance.
The near-controlled parameter comparison makes shaping the leading explanation.
Single seeds and training stochasticity could still account for some difference.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether defense-biasing the slight shaping potential reverses the unbiased shaping regression.

results_insights.insight: Defense weight 1.5 raised average win rate from 27% to 45%.
Defensive-X rose from 30% to 80%, over 14.09-move games.
Improvement occurred without longer defensive episodes.

reasoning: Defense weight 1.5 corrected much of the unbiased shaping regression and exceeded the unshaped average.
The controlled defense-weight delta strongly links the gain to defense-biased shaping.
Combined-O remained only 4%, so the gain was not uniformly distributed; seed variance remains.

runs.goal_hypothesis: Test whether raising defense weight from 1.5 to 2.0 further improves robust combined-heuristic performance.

results_insights.insight: Defensive-X decreased from 80% to 72%, over 12.77-move games.
The higher weight shortened defensive-X games but did not improve wins.

reasoning: Increasing defense weight to 2.0 produced only a negligible average gain and worse robustness.
Weight 1.5 appears a better balance across matchups than 2.0.
The average difference is smaller than plausible evaluation/training noise, so no causal improvement should be claimed.
